text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Cuts to bad debt provisions and higher interest income helped lift Westpac Banking Corp's annual net profit to A$1.132 billion, a 20 per cent gain. Still, managing director Bob Joss predicted a tougher year in 1997, expecting continued tightening of home loan margins as more securitising and more origination is done "off a bank's balance sheet, as opposed to on". Page 1.

The world's biggest stockbroker, Merrill Lynch, yesterday gave itself a powerful base from which to build a potentially dominant position in the local stockbroking scene with the A$117 million purchase of one of Australia's leading brokers, McIntosh Securties. Merrill Lynch's corporate strategy chief, Jerry Kenney, said the firm would aim to lift McIntosh into the number one or two spot in Australia, from its present rank of around number five. Page 1.

Mobil Oil Australia will consider cancelling John Holland construction group's contract to build a massive new A$250 million catalytic cracker at Mobil's Altona refinery in Melbourne, following long delays and possible cost blowouts because of poor industial relations, inclement weather and management problems on the project. Page 3.

News Corp yesterday reported a first-quarter net profit after abnormals of A$283 million after takings from the hit film Independence Day boosted operating income for the Fox film division from A$40 million in the previous corresponding quarter to A$96 milion. Page 21.

Some large investors confirmed yesterday they would support a recommendation in an Independent Shareholder Services report which advised against the re-election of former Coles Myer chairman Solomon Lew, after the report reinforced shareholder concerns abut the company's handling of the Yannon share deal. Page 21.

Mayne Nickless Ltd chairman Ian Webber told the company's annual general meeting in Melbourne yesterday that it was still pursuing a float of Optus Communications before the end of this calendar year, but details of the float could not be revealed because of outstanding matters such as the Seven Network's decision to seek a court ruling on its shareholders' agreement with Optus Vision. Page 22.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Despite contributions from the hit film Independence Day, the News Corp yesterday reported a flat net profit of A$285 million for the first quarter of the financial year, compared to A$284 million the previous year, partly because of a drop in earnings at the United States TV business and Australian newspapers. Page 31.

Westpac Banking Corp Ltd and St George Bank Ltd announced better than expected annual profits yesterday, but the banks still forecast a gloomy year head, with competition from non-bank lenders expected to intensify. Westpac reported a net profit after tax and before abnormals of A$1.13 billion in the 12 months to September 30 and St George reported a net profit of A$166 million. Page 31.

Now Australia's biggest regional broadcaster, Prime TV said yesterday it expected to lift Golden West Network operating earnings by 40 per cent to more than A$10 million within 18 months after buying the West Australian TV network from Kerry Stokes for A$71 million. Page 31.

The West Australian Government has approved Kingstream Resources NL's A$1.4 billion Mid West Iron and Steel Project after receiving a commitment from Kingstream and its Taiwanese partner, An Feng Steel, to move the steel plant from Geraldton to Oakajee, a proposed industrial site 25km north of the coastal city. Page 31.

Mayne Nickless Ltd told yesterday's annual meeting that the group was committed to a float of Optus Communications before December, despite delays caused by litigation between Seven and Optus Vision. Seven, a shareholder in Optus Vision, claims a deal beween Optus Vision and Publishing & Broadcasting Ltd is in breach of the original shareholders' agreement for the pay TV group. Page 33.

Boosted by stronger residential and commercial lending, St George Bank Ltd yesterday reported a 17.9 per cent rise in net profit after tax and before abnormals from A$141.1 million to A$166.3 million in the year to September 30. However, investors sold St George shares 15 cents lower to A$8.51, reacting to the forecast of a tough year ahead by managing director Jim Sweeney. Page 33.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

After announcing a 19.5 per cent gain in net annual profit to A$1.13 billion, Westpac Banking Corporation managing director Robert Joss yesterday signalled a renewed efficiency drive to ensure the bank continues to achieve earnings growth. A A$209 million drop in the charge for bad debts to A$121 million accounted for 70 per cent of the rise in net profit. Page 29.

News Corp yesterday posted a disappointing eight per cent fall in net profit to A$283 million for the three months to September. Despite a 140 per cent jump in operating profit from News' filmed entertainment business from A$40 million to A$96 million, operating income from the television division was down from A$111 million to A$67 million. Page 29.

Despite uncertainty over its programming arrangements and the possibility of future competition, Prime Television yesterday agreed to buy Golden West Network from Kerry Stokes' privately owned Australian Capital Equity for A$71 million. If the AustralianCompetition and Consumer Commission wins a legal battle with GWN and the Seven Network, GWN will lose the right to receive Nine Network programming on an exclusive basis - undermining its value. Page 29.

Despite reporting a 9.4 per cent rise in annual net profit to A$148.3 million, St George Bank warned shareholders yesterday that they should expect a flatter result next year as lending profit margins become tighter in the intensely competitive market. St George will pay a final dividend of 26 cents per ordinary share, fully franked at 36 per cent. Page 31.

Three key directors of McIntosh Securities, John McIntosh, Bruce Parncutt and Bill Conn, will together make about A$21 million by accepting a A$1.40-a-share cash offer from US securities house Merrill Lynch. The agreed A$117 million takeover bid would remove one of Australia's last remaining large independent brokers. Page 31.

Although the planned float of Optus Communications has experienced delays because of legal action taken by the Seven Network against a shareholding arrangement between Optus Vision and Kerry Packer's Publishing & Broadcasting and the Federal Government's ejection of a bid by Optus' foreign shareholders to gain more voting power, Mayne Nickless chairman Ian Webber is confident the A$4 billion float will be concluded this calendar year. Page 31.
THE AGE

Westpac has become the fourth of Australia's big banks to join the billion-dollar club, after posting a 19.5 per cent improvement in profit to A$1.13 billion in the year to September. Westpac managing director Bob Joss acknowledged that bad debts were prbably at their lowest point in the credit cycle, making further gains in profitability from this source unlikely. Page C1.

After launching an agreed A$117 million takeover bid for McIntosh Securities yesterday, US securities house Merrill Lynch said it had already picked up 19.15 per cent of the company through options trading on Sunday, but so far it had failed to secure the upport of ING, the Dutch banking group which owns 19.7 per cent of McIntosh. Page C1.

News Corporation's share price dropped to A$6.95 yesterday after an unexpected slump in earnings by Fox Television and News' other broadcasting interests in the United States. The world-wide box office success of the film Independence Day and strong operating performances from its British newspaper group and its US magazines proved to be News' only salvation, giving the group a flat profit of A$285 million for the first quarter. Page C3.

A survey by the Australian Bureau of Statistics showed yesterday that the rapid growth of Australia's research and development program had slowed significantly even before the Federal Government decided to cut support for R&D in the August Budget. After rising from 1.26 per cent of GDP in 1988-89 to 1.59 per cent by 1992-93, the survey revealed the share rose to just 1.61 per cent two years later. Page C3.

Ansell's sales to the largest alliance of hospitals and health systems in the United States are set to more than double, after the health-care and protective products unit of Pacific Dunlop won a five-year, A$120 million contract to supply surgical and exmination gloves to Premier Inc. Page C3.

Ten Network shareholder TNQ yesterday sold its 14.9 per cent stake in regional broadcaster Telecasters Australia at A$6.50-a-share. Telecasters was formed by the merger of the Queensland regional television operations of Telecasters North Queensland and he northern New South Wales regional television operations of Northern Rivers Television. Page C3.
